subject: RE: Deployment mode follow-up — SSO / KMS / Logging retention
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode follow-up — SSO / KMS / Logging retention

Hi Samantha — thanks again for the demo and discussion today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can converge on whether Dedicated or a Private VPC is the right fit for Acme: 

Recap:
- Primary concern: sensitive PII + regulated workflows for payments reconciliation.
- Requirements you highlighted: enterprise SSO with SCIM + IdP-initiated SAML, customer-managed KMS/HSM integration for key custody, and 7 years of immutable logging with SOC2-grade retention controls.
- Traffic profile: steady 60 qps average, 250 qps peak during batch windows (ETL jobs).

Initial qualification thoughts:
- Hosted API: fast to start but won’t meet KMS/HSM or private-networking requirements.
- Dedicated capacity: can provide dedicated GPU pools and isolation, supports some KMS integrations (depending on model) and regionally isolated instances — but full customer-managed HSM + strict log immutability typically points toward Private.
- Private VPC / On‑prem: provides network isolation, full KMS/HSM integration, and tighter logging/retention controls, but longer lead time and procurement.

Next steps I propose:
1) Can you confirm whether Acme requires HSM-backed key custody (FIPS 140-2/3) for model encryption at rest, or if CMEK in your cloud KMS is sufficient?
2) If HSM is required, can Brandon (cc’d) share the standard onboarding checklist ACME Security uses so our infra team can map controls?
3) I’ll loop in our solutions engineer (Neha) to propose an architecture for Dedicated vs Private that meets SSO/KMS/logging constraints — target delivery by EOD Friday.

I’ve attached a brief checklist we typically use for SSO/KMS/logging intake. Happy to hop on a quick call if that’s easier.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

marissa@redwood.com

Thanks Marissa — helpful summary. Quick answers: 

- We do require HSM-backed key custody for anything that could decrypt PII outside our control; CMEK alone is not sufficient for the security team.
- Brandon — can you paste the onboarding checklist? Also, what retention format do you need for logs (we retain logs in WORM format for 7 years).
- Legal will need to review any data processing addendum and the SLA if we go Private.

Happy to do a 30m follow-up Monday to review the architecture Neha proposes.

Best,
Samantha Li
Head of Data Governance | Acme Corp
Samantha.Li@acmecorp.com

Hi Samantha — looping in technical notes based on your HSM requirement. High-level options: 

Option A — Private VPC / On‑prem (recommended for HSM + WORM logging):
- Full network isolation; customer-managed HSM (BYOK) integrated via KMIP/HSM proxy.
- We can ship an on‑prem gateway or deploy in your VPC with our Private control plane.
- Logging: support for immutable WORM buckets (S3 Object Lock) and long-term export to your archival store; we can centralize audit logs in your SIEM.
- Tradeoffs: procurement (infra + support) and 4–8 week deployment timeline.

Option B — Dedicated (fast, partial fit):
- Dedicated GPU pools in a tenant-isolated cluster; supports CMEK and cloud KMS with limited HSM passthrough depending on region and partner HSM support.
- Logging retention configurable, but immutable WORM guarantees and long-term archival under your tenancy require Private deployment.
- Tradeoffs: lower lead time (1–2 weeks), but may need legal exceptions for HSM & log immutability.

Action items I can take this week:
- Draft architecture diagrams for both options with integration points for SCIM/SAML, KMS/HSM (KMIP/PKCS11), and logging export paths.
- Identify any feature gaps that would require product exceptions.

Marissa — if you confirm Monday call, I’ll bring a short diagram and a checklist mapping to Acme’s onboarding items.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com
